name: Oyster Soup
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: One quart or twenty-five oysters in their own liquor

ingredients.name: One cupful of scalded milk or cream

ingredients.originalText: Pepper, salt if necessary, and a dash of cayenne or paprica

instructions.text: Scald a quart or twenty-five oysters in their own liquor
As soon as they are plump, or the gills curl, remove them
Add to the liquor a cupful of water
Make a roux of one tablespoonful each of butter and flour, dilute it with the liquor, and when it is smooth add a cupful of scalded milk or cream
Season with pepper, salt if necessary, and a dash of cayenne or paprica
Add the oysters, and as soon as they are heated serve at once
Examine oysters carefully, and pass the liquor through a fine sieve before being cooked, in order to remove any pieces of shell

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Scald a quart or twenty-five oysters in their own liquor
2. As soon as they are plump, or the gills curl, remove them
3. Add to the liquor a cupful of water
4. Make a roux of one tablespoonful each of butter and flour, dilute it with the liquor, and when it is smooth add a cupful of scalded milk or cream
5. Season with pepper, salt if necessary, and a dash of cayenne or paprica
6. Add the oysters, and as soon as they are heated serve at once
7. Examine oysters carefully, and pass the liquor through a fine sieve before being cooked, in order to remove any pieces of shell
